text: Every Bicep resource declaration follows the same shape: a symbolic name, a resource type string with its API version, and a body of properties.
The symbolic name isn't the Azure resource's actual name — it's what other parts of the file use to reference this resource. The real Azure name is the name property inside the body.
Bicep is a friendlier syntax over the exact same deployment engine. The resource compiles down to the same ARM template JSON — same type, same API version, same properties.

Bicep infers a dependency automatically whenever one resource references another's symbolic name — no explicit dependsOn needed. The Visualizer renders that exact graph live, generated from the file you're looking at.
Same deployment engine, friendlier syntax, a live graph to check your work. Next up: parameters and variables in Bicep.
